rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (kp 2.0, kd 1.5, base_speed 0.9, sensors at y=0.08, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6 kg) is the best design so far at 473.6. Its oval finishes 18 of 20 (mean 1.91 s), its s-bend finishes 6 of 20 (progress 0.74), and its slalom always ends off track at progress about 0.15. Each finished run is worth roughly 900 points, so converting s-bend runs is the main lever. Iteration 7 (kp 2.4, kd 1.0) overshot on the s-bend and scored 431. Iteration 9 (base_speed 0.85) lost s-bend finishes and scored 429, so 0.9 stays. Iteration 10 (kd 2.0) returned metrics identical to iteration 8, so kd above 1.5 showed no measurable effect and the kd 1.5 point is the best-supported. Sensors are already at the forward limit (y=0.08), and the off-track floor of 0.06 m cannot be widened by body width.

Change: kp raised from 2.0 to 2.2, with kd held at 1.5 and everything else unchanged from iteration 8. The kd 1.5 damping should absorb part of the extra proportional gain that overshot at kp 2.4 with kd 1.0. The step is small, so it tests whether a firmer correction helps the s-bend without the oscillation seen at 2.4. At a full edge signal of 2, turn is 4.4, giving about 1540 PWM of differential, which stays below the base PWM of about 1843 at speed 0.9, so the wheels do not reverse.

Expected result: oval completion stays at about 90 percent or better, s-bend finishes hold at 6 or more of 20, and steering oscillation stays near 0.37. Score target is about 475 to 520. Main risk: kp 2.2 overshoots on the s-bend as kp 2.4 did, in which case the revision should revert to kp 2.0.
